description: Tail-shape and tail-width regime sweep on the Gumbel pivot.  Every rule is calibrated once on the exact null and applied unchanged to six shape laws, five inside the Dirichlet family and one (the released simulator's normalised-uniform tail) outside it, and four restricted-width laws.
seed_note: Fresh seed, distinct from 240401245 (clean benchmark), 240401246 (contamination), 240401247 (contamination quadrature check), 240401248 (deficit sweep) and 240401249 (short-horizon probe).

alpha.note: inf is the equal-tail (spike) limit stated by Li et al. (2025). The grid is frozen before simulation and is never a function of the regime.

rules.name: bayes_shared_spike
rules.note: the manuscript's existing shared-Delta Gumbel Bayes rule; the equal-tail spike component

rules.name: bayes_shared_dirichlet_mixture
rules.note: the method added by this section

rules.name: bayes_shared_uniontail
rules.note: A document-level union of the full-width Dirichlet shape branch and the closed-form width branch at J < K. The equal-tail spike is the alpha=inf atom in the shape branch.

competitor_scope: Best-rule and regret summaries are relative only to the configured finite rule menu. Point-alpha competitors are exactly config.point_alphas plus the alpha=inf spike; alpha-grid atoms used inside the mixture are not automatically point-rule competitors. This is not an optimization over all positive alpha or all priors.

tail_width_layer.hierarchy_scope: This records the hierarchies evaluated, not a general claim that tokenwise mixtures cannot improve power.
tail_width_layer.why_gumbel_only: The working inverse limiting alternative depends on Delta alone.
tail_width_layer.component: A union of a full-width Dirichlet tail-shape branch and an equal-weight live-tail-width branch restricted to J < V-1. The width component is f_{Delta,J}(r) = r**(Delta/(1-Delta)) + J*r**(J/Delta-1). The shape component uses the tabulated psi_alpha transform.

tail_width_prior.family: uniform on the configured ladder strictly below V-1
tail_width_prior.note: The equal-tail atom (alpha=inf, J=V-1) belongs to the shape branch. It is excluded from the width branch to avoid counting the full-width atom twice.

normalisation.note: Both branches integrate to one analytically. The width formula is closed form; the shape implementation interpolates a transform table. Tokenwise scoring, when requested, also uses outer lookups. Numerical mass and node-sensitivity checks are not certificates that the evaluated densities have mass at most one. The exact test-martingale result requires conditional null validity and analytic or certified normalized evaluation; it is not asserted for these interpolated implementations.

prior_fingerprint.family: union of the Dirichlet tail-shape and tail-width families

containment_check.note: Recorded discrepancy for the equal-tail atom in the interpolated shape branch; not an exact arithmetic identity.

metadata_correction.scope: Description corrected from the stored union prior fingerprint; numerical results unchanged.

T1.description: equal tail (alpha -> inf); the specification stated by Li et al. (2025) and the generator behind every other Gumbel result in this study

T2.description: Dirichlet(10) tail; mildly dispersed, close to the equal-tail limit

T3.description: Dirichlet(3) tail; variance-matched to the released simulator's normalized-uniform tail, and not an atom of the frozen alpha prior

T4.description: Dirichlet(0.5) tail; sparse, and deliberately NOT an atom of the frozen alpha prior, and further from every atom than T3

T5.description: Dirichlet(0.1) tail; strongly sparse, most of the deficit on a few coordinates

T6.description: tail built by normalising i.i.d. uniforms, as in the released simulator of Li et al. (2025); OUTSIDE the Dirichlet family at every alpha

W1.description: deficit on a single tail coordinate; the width fitted on the released outputs

W2.description: deficit spread equally over 4 tail coordinates

W3.description: deficit spread equally over 16 tail coordinates

W4.description: deficit spread equally over 64 tail coordinates; approaching the full width

calibration.sample: one exact-null sample shared by every regime
calibration.note: The Gumbel pivot null is Uniform(0,1) and does not depend on the alternative's tail, so one calibration sample legitimately serves all configured regimes; the evaluation null is a fresh, separate sample.

max_regret_mc_se_method.resampling: Documents are resampled independently within each generating tail law and jointly across all rules and horizons.  Each draw recomputes the best rule within every tail law and then the maximum regret across tail laws.
max_regret_mc_se_method.excluded_uncertainty: Calibration-sample, quadrature, finite-menu selection and model uncertainty are not included.
